sample_unit: lesions (302 patients); 150-lesion subset read by 4 readers

links.outcome: Reader diagnostic performance (AUC) and agreement with vs without LLM assistance, junior vs senior
links.effect: Juniors with LLM: weighted κ ≥ 0.85, mean ΔAUC = 0.10 (p = 0.06, non-significant); seniors ΔAUC = 0.01 (p = 0.22). Gains reflect reliance on LLM rather than independent skill.
links.quote: In contrast, senior readers showed stable performance (mean ΔAUC = 0.01; p = 0.22).

links.outcome: Acceptance of LLM suggestions in discordant cases by reader experience level
links.effect: Junior readers accepted LLM suggestions in 60.78%-72.34% of discordant cases versus 2.04%-2.33% among seniors.
links.quote: In discordant cases, junior readers accepted LLM suggestions in 60.78%-72.34% of instances, compared with only 2.04%-2.33% among seniors.

screen.reason: The study evaluated large language models in assisting junior and senior radiologists to interpret ultrasound reports using a crossover design with and without LLM assistance.

primary.practice: AI-assisted clinical interpretation compared to unassisted reading
